author: Akihiro-Tabuchi
title: Debian Packages job fails - apt cannot reach azure.archive.ubuntu.com (network timeout)
signature: Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com connection timed out|Network

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: apt-get update fails with connection timeout to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80

key_errors:
Err:1 http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble InRelease
  Could not connect to azure.archive.ubuntu.com:80 (52.250.76.244), connection timed out

E: Package 'gnupg' has no installation candidate
E: Unable to locate package wget
E: Package 'ca-certificates' has no installation candidate
root_cause: The apt-get update step in the Debian Packages job failed to reach azure.archive.ubuntu.com (IP 52.250.76.244) on port 80. All four Ubuntu mirror InRelease endpoints (noble, noble-updates, noble-backports, noble-security) returned connection timeouts after multiple retries over ~4 minutes. This is a transient network/infrastructure failure on the Azure-hosted GitHub Actions runner - the Azure Ubuntu package mirror was unreachable from the runner at the time of the job, causing package index updates to fail and subsequently preventing installation of gnupg, wget, ca-certificates, and lsb-release.
reproduction_steps: N/A - infrastructure/network issue not reproducible outside CI
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed Debian Packages job - the network issue is transient
If the failure recurs, investigate Azure CDN/mirror outage status
Consider adding retry logic to apt-get update in the Debian Packages workflow
prevention_strategies: Add retry logic (e.g., apt-get update with retries or use a fallback mirror) in the Debian Packages job to handle transient Azure mirror outages.
historical_context: This is an Azure runner network timeout to the Ubuntu package mirror - a known transient infrastructure issue that can affect any Ubuntu-based CI job.
